answer: In an agent economy trading goods from velvet to software, every identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for work. Agents can wander between sellers, but each account needs its own bond. A sudden pulse of new identities therefore ties up capital: an attacker running 1,000 accounts must immobilize 100,000 tokens. The rule does not prove uniqueness; it makes multiplying identities expensive.
